abstract: Oversees marine protected area boundary verifications and environmental permitting
system_message:
You are the Environmental and maritime compliance officer (MCOMP). Your primary responsibilities include overseeing marine protected area boundary verifications and environmental permitting, as well as tracking vessel effluent treatment monitoring across candidate oceanographic research transects.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Vessel effluent treatment monitoring（WASTE）
information_points.content:
MCOMP-WASTE-F1H：Regarding the Porcupine Abyssal Plain Station, the MARPOL environmental compliance audit of the research vessel marine sanitation system records a treated greywater surge tank margin of 40 m3 of reserve holding capacity prior to required offshore processing.
MCOMP-WASTE-ADE：Regarding the Charlie-Gibbs Fracture Zone Deep, the vessel marine sanitation audit shows a treated greywater surge tank margin of 55 m3 of reserve holding tank volume prior to mandatory offshore processing.
MCOMP-WASTE-ZG3：Regarding the Hatton-Rockall Trough Transect, the MARPOL environmental compliance audit reports a treated greywater surge tank margin of 25 m3 remaining in reserve holding capacity for the vessel sanitation system.

information_points.title: Oversees marine protected area boundary verifications and environmental permitting（PERMIT）
information_points.content:
MCOMP-PERMIT-ARE：For the Hatton-Rockall Trough Transect, the high-seas regulatory jurisdiction review covering the transect coordinates and surrounding 12 nautical mile corridor indicates that the marine protected area buffer is not cleared, as survey lines do not fully lie outside restricted ecological preserves.
MCOMP-PERMIT-CIA：For the Porcupine Abyssal Plain Station, the high-seas regulatory jurisdiction review of the transect coordinates and surrounding 12 nautical mile corridor confirms that the marine protected area buffer is cleared, with all survey lines lying fully outside restricted ecological preserves.
MCOMP-PERMIT-R28：For the Charlie-Gibbs Fracture Zone Deep, the high-seas regulatory jurisdiction review confirms that the marine protected area buffer is cleared across the transect coordinates and surrounding 12 nautical mile corridor.
